main_result.description: For the specified queue and recipient behavior, successful withdrawals in the modeled Lido path preserve the withdrawal reserve. Failed withdrawals restore the modeled transaction state. These results depend on the stated configuration, storage, arithmetic and funding conditions.
main_result.model: Source transaction interpreter using Verity physical contract storage; not a full Verity EVM execution theorem

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Source.TrioReserve1.PhysicalReserve.success_preserves
theorems.doc:
/-- Concrete successful execution preserves the independent protected reserve
on the resulting physical world, and its next live queue read returns the same
demand. Every execution premise is a physical/configuration or numeric check. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem success_preserves (k : Queue.Keccak) (c : Config) (staticOther : StaticCall.External)
    (other : External) (ctx : Context) (w : World) (amount seeds : Word)
    (demand reference deadline time : Nat) (b : Bound c ctx w)
    (hb : Queue.isBunkerModeActive c.contracts.queue w = false)
    (hp : (w.core.readContractSlot ctx.self.val activeSlot).val ≠ 0)
    (hauth : ctx.sender = c.contracts.router) (hn : amount.val ≠ 0)
    (hq : Queue.unfinalizedStETH k c.contracts.queue w = .ok demand)
    (hamount : amount.val ≤ (QueueCalls.allocationValues ctx w demand).deposits +
      (QueueCalls.allocationValues ctx w demand).unreserved)
    (hf : Consensus.compute c.frame (prepared ctx amount w demand).core.blockTimestamp.val
      ((prepared ctx amount w demand).core.readContractSlot c.consensus.val c.frame.frameSlot).val =
        .ok (reference, deadline))
    (ht : Oracle.timestamp c.oracle.genesis.val c.oracle.secondsPerSlot.val reference = .value time)
    (hseed : ((spent ctx amount w demand reference).core.readContractSlot ctx.self.val seedSlot).val % width +
      seeds.val < Verity.Core.UINT256_MODULUS)
    (hfunds : amount.val ≤ w.balances ctx.self)
    (hlido : ctx.self = c.lido) (hrcode : (w.core.codeSize c.contracts.router.val).val ≠ 0)
    (hqueue : c.contracts.queue.val ≠ ctx.self.val) :
    let result := run (withdrawDepositableEther (external k c staticOther other) ctx amount seeds) w
    result.outcome = .ok () ∧
      buffer ctx result.world = buffer ctx w - amount.val ∧
      reserve ctx result.world = reserve ctx w - amount.val ∧
      Queue.unfinalizedStETH k c.contracts.queue result.world = .ok demand ∧
      PartitionSpec.protectedReserve (buffer ctx result.world) (reserve ctx result.world) demand =
        PartitionSpec.protectedReserve (buffer ctx w) (reserve ctx w) demand

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Source.TrioComposition.ReserveLeafSpend.withdrawal_corresponds
theorems.doc:
/-- Exhaustive parent equivalence, including every revert and transaction
rollback. No allocation/frame execution equality remains in this independent
parent relation, and no callee success or desired reserve property is assumed. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem withdrawal_corresponds (external : External) (ctx : Context) (amount seeds : Word)
    (before after : World) (outcome : Except Fault Unit) (trace : List Attempt) :
    Withdrawal external ctx amount seeds before outcome after trace ↔
      run (withdrawDepositableEther external ctx amount seeds) before = ⟨outcome,after,trace⟩

covered: Withdrawal correspondence covers ordered status and permission checks, live queue and frame reads, partition arithmetic and recipient effects.
The specified physical queue, consensus and recipient pipeline preserves the independent protected reserve on success.
The withdrawal specification restores the pre-transaction world on failure; attempted calls remain observable.
missing: Reserve protection does not cover arbitrary successful callbacks.
The transaction interpreter uses Verity contract storage, but full correspondence with Verity EVM execution and deployed callees is not established.
Sequence results cover only the modeled transitions, not every queue writer, migration or report path.
conditions: Compiler interpretation of aligned, non-overlapping observed word loads/stores and copies; omitted private cache/configuration/scratch writes obey the stated frame and cache-field relations.

Configured linked library identity, storage/hash interpretation, entry pointer provenance and primitive crypto/consensus bindings are explicit; general compiled/deployed-code and gas verification are excluded.

Concrete-pipeline protection takes physical address/code bindings, admitted amount, queue/frame computations, seed arithmetic, funding and queue/Lido separation. Balance credit bounds use an explicit aggregate-world bound. Sequence claims cover the modeled internal/committed transitions only.
outside: Compiled and deployed bytecode, gas costs and full consensus-state truth.

summary: The executable parent actual_reserve_physical_history consumes finite histories of existing target/rebalance writers, guarded report accounting and guarded withdrawal, threading each actual returned World. Its shared callee uses concrete Keccak and physical queue finalization/getters plus locator/router/oracle/consensus producers. Successful withdrawal derives the actual spending-stage partition from locator/queue-return bytes and admission. Source-stage rollback and report accounting consume their actual producer results. Configured deployment identities, target outer ACL and final arbitrary-callback preservation remain explicit boundaries; historical cache-scoped source/legacy Verity theorems are retained. Under A-NO-REENTRY, PReserve1NoReentry derives the final reserve word of a successful withdrawal from the spending stage. Reserve-target access control (2026-09-18): PReserve1TargetAdmission composes the setter's Aragon role check (kernel/ACL CALL) as an admission stage of the physical writer history.

classification.work: Validate the registered physical writer/callee history and reconcile final checks. Keep exact deployment/outer-entry/final-callback-preservation boundaries; never substitute a cached demand or supplied successful-call record for a producer.

No global deployed reserve invariant is certified.

theorems.name: LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PReserve1.source_spend_preserves_withdrawal_reserve
theorems.doc:
/-- **P-RESERVE-1, source plane.** Under a fresh withdrawal-queue cache, any
committed `withdrawDepositableEther` spend passed the scoped guards, spent a
nonzero amount, took it from the depositable partitions only, and left the live
queue-facing withdrawals reserve unchanged.

Registered Wave 1 parent for P-RESERVE-1. Strengthened along the three
axes `report/P-RESERVE-1.md` calls out (issues #1, #2, #5):

* the premise is `modelWithdrawDepositableEther`, the full wrapper
  transition that enforces `canDeposit`/`authorizedRouter`
  (`scopedWithdrawGuards`) and the `amount ≠ 0` (`ZERO_AMOUNT`) guard before
  ever reaching `_spendDepositableEther`, not the bare internal spend helper
  the original theorem quoted. The conclusion now *proves*
  `scopedWithdrawGuards inputs` and `amount ≠ 0`, rather than assuming them: a
  guard failure reverts, so it can never reach the `.committed` branch this
  theorem is about;
* the conclusion adds `liveEffectiveWithdrawalsReserve after live =
  liveEffectiveWithdrawalsReserve before live`, the *effective*, min-capped,
  queue-facing reserve computed against an explicit `live` value standing in
  for a `WithdrawalQueue.unfinalizedStETH()` CALL — not merely the restated
  `storedDepositsReserve` field that `withdrawalPartitionSpendInvariant`
  quotes;
* that added conjunct needs `freshQueueCache before live`, naming the
  cache-freshness the original theorem left implicit. Drop that hypothesis
  and the identical spend from `depositsReserve + unreserved` can still raid
  the live reserve — see `staleQueueCacheKillLine_holds` and
  `LidoSRv3.Tests.ReserveMutants.stale_queue_cache_mutant_counterexample` for
  the concrete premise-necessity witness (it refutes the freshness-dropped
  sibling claim, i.e. shows the hypothesis cannot be removed; it does not
  refute this parent, which cannot be instantiated on that stale-cache
  vector).

The parent kill-lines, one per conjunct group, each the negation of this
theorem's full predicate shape — all five binders, `freshQueueCache`
hypothesis retained, same three-conjunct conclusion — applied to a mutant of
`modelWithdrawDepositableEther`:

* `LidoSRv3.Tests.ReserveMutants.guard_drop_kill_line_refutes_parent` kills
  conjunct (1) (`scopedWithdrawGuards` guard liveness): the mutant
  `mutantWithdrawNoCanDeposit` deletes only the `canDeposit` check, so on the
  witness (`canDeposit = false`, `authorizedRouter = true`, nonzero amount,
  fresh cache) the mutated call commits while the first conjunct is false.
* `LidoSRv3.Tests.ReserveMutants.partition_spend_mutant_kill_line_refutes_parent`
  kills conjuncts (2)-(3): the mutant `mutantWithdraw` keeps every guard and
  mutates the spend transition (`withdrawalPartitionMutant` commits the
  spend, then overwrites `buffered` with the post-spend
  `storedDepositsReserve`). On the witness vector the mutated call commits
  under a fresh cache while the live queue-facing reserve drops 50 → 0.

The original `withdrawalPartitionSpendInvariant` conjunct is retained so
existing consumers of this theorem name keep their evidence. -/
theorems.statement:
theorem source_spend_preserves_withdrawal_reserve
    (inputs : WithdrawInputs) (before after : ReserveState) (amount live : Word)
    (hfresh : freshQueueCache before live)
    (h : modelWithdrawDepositableEther inputs before amount = .committed after) :
    scopedWithdrawGuards inputs ∧
      amount ≠ 0 ∧
      withdrawalPartitionSpendInvariant before after amount ∧
      liveEffectiveWithdrawalsReserve after live = liveEffectiveWithdrawalsReserve before live

assumptions.risk: The external callees reached by the modeled Lido, StakingRouter and gateway executions -- module obtainDepositData bodies, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 consolidation-request predeploy, the WithdrawalQueue finalization callback and the configured refund recipient -- do not call back into Lido, the router or the gateway. `LidoSRv3/Audit/Source/NoReentry.lean` names this on the Live external-call interpreter as `NoReentry (external : External) (self : List Address)`: a call targeting a protected address is rejected, an accepted reply returns a world agreeing with the received world on every protected address (all storage words and the balance), and no recorded nested attempt into a protected address was accepted. A callee that re-enters (for example a malicious module implementation or a refund recipient that calls back into the gateway) is not covered.
assumptions.justification: Thomas 2026-09-17 (step 1b of the "not proven" cleanup): the deployed callees are audited protocol contracts, the beacon deposit contract and an EIP predeploy, so their non-re-entry may be assumed rather than proved per body. The registry prose at `audit/topup-call-history/README.md:51` argued that adding a `noReentry` premise would not close the TOPUP-2 per-block cap; the owner overrides that reading for the five rows below, where the premise constrains only the callee interpreter of theorems that already thread the exact returned world, and where the corollaries are stated on those theorems. Corollaries: `PDeposit1NoReentry.actual_physical_metadata_conserves_no_reentry` (DEPOSIT-1 ledger plus `Confined other [lido, router]`), `PTopup1NoReentry.actual_continuation_locator_conserves_no_reentry` (TOPUP-1), `PReserve1NoReentry.actual_reserve_history_final_reserve` (RESERVE-1: the final reserve word equals the spending stage's), `PConsolidationEth1NoReentry.settlement_preserves_gateway_and_vault_storage` (ETH-1: gateway and vault storage equal the post-quota storage after the inbox and refund CALLs) and `PAddress1NoReentry.claim_returns_committed_storage` / `actual_claim_batch_no_reentry` (ADDRESS-1: the claimed bit and locked-ether write survive the recipient CALL; no accepted nested call into the queue). The generic consequences for `Live.call` are `call_storage`, `call_balance`, `call_self_rejected` and `call_nested_rejects`.
assumptions.violation_impact: If a callee re-enters Lido, the router or the gateway, the corollaries above do not apply: the final reserve, the gateway/vault storage after settlement, the claimed bit after a recipient CALL and the confinement of module/beacon calls are no longer derived, and the exact-returned-world parents must be consulted with the re-entrant world.
assumptions.validation: `lake build LidoSRv3.Audit.Source.NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PDeposit1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PTopup1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PReserve1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PConsolidationEth1NoReentry LidoSRv3.Audit.Guarantees.PAddress1NoReentry` checks the corollaries. The premise itself is validated only by review of the pinned callee sources (NodeOperatorsRegistry/CSM obtainDepositData, deposit_contract.sol, the EIP-7251 predeploy, WithdrawalQueue.finalize, the refund recipient configuration); it is not proved for the deployed runtimes.
assumptions.removal_path: Prove `NoReentry` for each deployed callee body: model obtainDepositData of NOR/CSM, the beacon deposit contract, the EIP-7251 predeploy and WithdrawalQueue.finalize as Live executables and show they issue no CALL into Lido, the router or the gateway; bind the refund recipient configuration. Then replace the premise by those theorems in the five corollaries.

covered: Registered actual_reserve_physical_history applies the full existing-operation history to QueueFinalize.dispatch concreteKeccak and Pipeline.external. Queue finalization and subsequent queue-demand/bunker getters share physical slots and the actual World; no freshQueueCache or caller-supplied successful staticcall record is a premise.

Each history step passes its actual result.world to the next. Target effects include min(reserve,requested), unchanged buffer/balances and ordered target/reserve events. Rebalance effects include max(reserve,target), unchanged buffer/target/balances and conditional event. These are internal source writers; no fabricated helper transition is substituted.

WithdrawSuccess inverts actual WithdrawalParent execution to obtain canDeposit/router/spend/tail worlds and traces, caller/nonzero admission and complete journal. spend_partition consumes actual allocation/require outcomes and obtains queue call/return/decoder, saved physical buffer/reserve and independent AllocationSpec.Describes.

ReportParent consumes ordered authorization/vault/finalization source stages and independent checked ReportAccounting. Physical queue finalization checks role/pause/range/deltas, writes checkpoints/lockedETH/finalized ID and emits its events before the report accounting/rebalance stage. Later failure restores the transaction entry World.

Original source_spend_preserves_withdrawal_reserve and verity_tx_simulates_reserve_spec remain with their original cache/model assumptions. The optional UnfinalizedStaticcall record bridge is not the producer used by this registration.
